record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.original_question: The forestry truck-routing problem differs from standard vehicle routing because it is a multi-period pickup-and-delivery problem with repeated visits to supply locations, lower and upper daily demand limits, driver change-overs, and loading constraints. The open question is how to formulate and solve this forestry-specific VRP exactly for industrial-scale instances, rather than relying only on heuristics.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7 How can we model and solve an exact formulation of the forestry VRP problem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following forestry truck-routing problem. Over a planning horizon of T consecutive days, a fleet of heterogeneous trucks must transport timber from a set S of supply locations (harvest sites) to a set D of demand locations (mills). The problem has the following features that distinguish it from the classical capacitated vehicle routing problem:

(i) Pickup and delivery: every truck trip consists of loading at some supply location s in S and unloading at some demand location d in D; trucks may perform multiple loaded trips per day.

(ii) Multi-period structure: the routing decisions span T days, and supply and demand quantities are defined per day.

(iii) Repeated visits: the same supply location may be visited many times within a single day and across days, by the same or different trucks.

(iv) Daily demand windows: for each demand location d and each day t, the total quantity delivered must lie in a prescribed interval [L_{d,t}, U_{d,t}] (lower and upper daily demand limits), rather than meeting an exact quantity.

(v) Driver change-overs: each truck is operated by drivers whose shifts are bounded by legal driving and working-time limits; drivers may be exchanged at designated change-over points, so a single truck route during one day may be served by a sequence of drivers subject to scheduling constraints.

(vi) Loading constraints: loading at a supply location requires a loader (machine or crew) with limited capacity per time unit, so simultaneous loadings at the same site are restricted, inducing time-coupling among trucks.

Design a mixed-integer programming formulation (e.g., arc-flow, commodity-flow, or set-partitioning/route-based) that exactly represents all of (i)–(vi), and develop an exact solution algorithm (such as branch-and-cut, branch-and-price, or branch-and-cut-and-price) capable of solving industrial-scale instances of this problem to proven optimality (or with a guaranteed optimality gap), rather than relying solely on heuristic or metaheuristic methods.
artifact.status_search_result: Literature on forestry/timber transportation routing (e.g., the Timber Transport VRP) presents heuristic and metaheuristic methods, and exact methods exist for various multi-period pickup-and-delivery VRP variants, but no published exact formulation and algorithm is reported that simultaneously handles all of the forestry-specific features (multi-period, repeated supply visits, daily demand intervals, driver change-overs, loader/loading constraints) at industrial scale. The problem therefore appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Timber Transport Vehicle Routing Problems: Formulation and Heuristic Solution
status_evidence.snippet: A model formulation and Tabu Search based solution method are presented for the Timber Transport Vehicle Routing Problem (TTVRP).
status_evidence.claim: Forestry timber transport VRP has been addressed primarily via heuristic methods (Tabu Search), not exact algorithms at industrial scale.

status_evidence.title: Exact Solution Methods for the Multi-Vehicle Multi-Period VRP
status_evidence.snippet: Exact branch-and-price methods for multi-period VRPs without forestry-specific constraints.
status_evidence.claim: Exact methods exist for general multi-period VRP but do not incorporate the full set of forestry constraints listed.
